key_insight: Raising cold-spray pressure from 30 to 60 bar increases copper particle velocity past the bonding threshold, producing denser, more ductile deposits with better conductivity but lower hardness.
engineering_relevance: For CSAM copper parts, spray pressure is a primary control knob to tune the trade-off between electrical performance, tensile ductility, and strength.
method: Cold-sprayed copper on a LightSPEE3D system at 30, 40, 50, and 60 bar
Measured particle/microstructural response with XRD and SEM
Evaluated performance using hardness, eddy current conductivity, and tensile testing
evidence_signal: The abstract reports progressive crystallite refinement and higher dislocation density with pressure, along with improved conductivity and a clear shift toward ductile tensile fracture at higher pressures.
watch_item: The optimum appears pressure-dependent for this specific system, so the same window may not transfer directly to other nozzle designs, feedstocks, or substrate conditions.
paper_title: Optimising Cold Spray Additive Manufacturing: Pressure-driven enhancement of mechanical performance in copper deposits
